query: For phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys, what single intervention could improve glass-forming ability and the thermal stability of the amorphous state? Formulate one testable hypothesis that specifies the intervention without presupposing its class, the mechanism by which it would act, the predicted improvement relative to an otherwise comparable baseline, the conditions under which it should or should not work, supporting prior evidence, and an experiment whose result would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing a small, controlled addition of boron into phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloys will promote better glass-forming ability and enhance the thermal stability of the resulting amorphous state.
generation.material_initial_state: Phosphorus-containing high-entropy or compositionally complex alloys that exhibit marginal glass forming ability and only moderate thermal stability in the amorphous state.
generation.intervention: Add 2–5 atomic percent boron to the alloy composition during synthesis.
generation.conditions: This improvement is expected when alloys are processed via rapid solidification routes under well-controlled mixing conditions; the beneficial effect may diminish if the boron content is too low to alter the structure or too high, which might lead to phase separation or embrittlement.
generation.structural_mediator: Boron’s incorporation leads to an increase in local atomic packing density and promotes enhanced short-range order (increased topological frustration) which hinders the formation of crystalline nuclei.
generation.mechanism: The boron atoms, due to their small size and bonding characteristics, disrupt the regular atomic arrangement, thereby reducing the mobility of atoms and impeding crystallization. This increases the critical cooling rate required for crystallization while also raising the glass transition temperature.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to the baseline alloy without boron, the boron-modified alloy is predicted to exhibit a lower critical cooling rate for glass formation and an elevated glass transition and/or crystallization onset temperature, indicating enhanced thermal stability of the amorphous state.
generation.baseline: The phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloy without any added boron.
generation.boundary: The beneficial effects are constrained within an optimal boron concentration range; deviations outside this range (either too little or too much boron) might not yield the desired improvements and could even negatively impact the mechanical properties.
generation.uncertainty: While the direction of the effect is anticipated based on boron’s role in enhancing short-range order, the precise optimal concentration and extent of the improvements in glass forming ability and thermal stability remain uncertain and might vary with different alloy systems and processing conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: Synthesize two sets of samples under identical rapid solidification conditions: one set of the baseline phosphorus-containing high-entropy alloy and another set with a 3 at.% boron addition. Characterize both sets for their glass forming ability and thermal stability.
measurements: Critical cooling rate for glass formation
Microstructural analysis (using TEM or SEM) to confirm the amorphous state
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the boron-added samples do not show a statistically significant reduction in the critical cooling rate and an increase in Tg and/or Tx compared to the baseline, then the hypothesis is falsified.
